questions.problem:
Find the least-squares solution to the system of linear equations given below. You're given that the columns of the corresponding coefficient matrix are linearly independent.

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=1 \\ 2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-1 \\ -{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}6 & 2 \\ 2 & 14\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{40}[\begin{aligned}7 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{20} \\ -\frac{1}{20}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the system $Ax=b$, where the matrix $A$ and the vector $b$ are shown below. Given that the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, find the minimum value of $‖Ax-b‖.$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 14 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 14 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}} \\ Ax & =b\end{aligned}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\,\,[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 14 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}15 \\ 15\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{15}[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ -1 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}15 \\ 15\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The minimum value of $‖Ax-b‖$ is attained when $x=\overset{^}{x},$ which is the least-squares solution of the system $Ax=b.$ In this case, $A\overset{^}{x}$ represents the orthogonal projection of $b$ onto the column space of $A,$ and $‖A\overset{^}{x}-b‖$ is the distance between the vector $b$ and the column space. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}A\overset{^}{x}-b & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 14 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -4 \\ -8 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
‖A\overset{^}{x}-b‖=\sqrt{{5}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+(-8)^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}=\sqrt{110}.
$$

questions.problem:
Given that the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, find the least-squares solution of $Ax=b$, where 

$\,$ $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 4 \\ 2 & -4 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,b=[\begin{aligned}12 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 12\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 4 \\ 2 & -4 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}12 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 12\end{aligned}]}}\end{aligned}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -4 & 0 & 4 \\ 4 & -2 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 4 \\ 2 & -4 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -4 & 0 & 4 \\ 4 & -2 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}12 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}16 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 32 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 24\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}48 \\ 48 \\ 24\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{96}[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}48 \\ 48 \\ 24\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ \frac{3}{2} \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the least-squares solution to the system of linear equations given below. You're given that the columns of the corresponding coefficient matrix are linearly independent.

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=8 \\ 4{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=2 \\ -4{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=2 \\ 4{x}_{1}-4{x}_{3}=-6\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 0 \\ 4 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & -4 & 2 \\ 4 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 2 \\ 2 \\ -6\end{aligned}]}}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 0 & 4 \\ -4 & 2 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 2 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 0 \\ 4 & 2 & 4 \\ 0 & -4 & 2 \\ 4 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 0 & 4 \\ -4 & 2 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 2 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}8 \\ 2 \\ 2 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}36 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 36 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 36\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -36 \\ 36\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{36}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ -36 \\ 36\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the system $Ax=b$, where the matrix $A$ and the vector $b$ are shown below. Given that the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, find the minimum value of $‖Ax-b‖.$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}} \\ Ax & =b\end{aligned}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\,\,[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}7 & 2 \\ 2 & 7\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}12 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{45}[\begin{aligned}7 & -2 \\ -2 & 7\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}12 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The minimum value of $‖Ax-b‖$ is attained when $x=\overset{^}{x},$ which is the least-squares solution of the system $Ax=b.$ In this case, $A\overset{^}{x}$ represents the orthogonal projection of $b$ onto the column space of $A,$ and $‖A\overset{^}{x}-b‖$ is the distance between the vector $b$ and the column space. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}A\overset{^}{x}-b & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
‖A\overset{^}{x}-b‖=\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{0}^{2}}=\sqrt{3}.
$$
